The `PromptTokenizer` implements a bounded reuse strategy that activates only when a specific message-end marker is present in the input text. It identifies the last occurrence of this marker and treats the text preceding it as a prefix for caching. This mechanism allows the system to avoid re-tokenizing identical conversational history, provided the tokenizer supports literal boundary splitting without normalization interference.

Cache eligibility requires the prefix to exceed a minimum character threshold and the marker to remain intact as a distinct token. If the prefix matches a cached entry, the system retrieves the associated token IDs, incrementing hit counters. When the prefix extends beyond a cached key, only the new segment is tokenized and appended. The system validates that the marker still terminates the prefix tokens; if an added token consumes part of the marker, the cache is bypassed to ensure correctness.

Storage is managed via an LRU cache constrained by both entry count and byte budget. Each entry stores the prefix string and its corresponding token IDs as binary data. The cache automatically evicts older entries when the total size exceeds the defined budget or when the maximum capacity is reached. This ensures that memory usage remains predictable while prioritizing recent conversational contexts for potential reuse.
